name: FlowTO
shortDescription: On-device digital twin of Toronto traffic on a DGX Spark: GNN demand prediction, cuGraph assignment and a Nemotron planning copilot.
description:
FlowTO is a city-scale traffic and transit digital twin of Toronto that runs entirely on-device on an NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10), with no cloud. Planners can simulate the network, drop interventions (closures, lane reductions, one-ways, signal retiming) snapped to real roads, and watch it recompute. The hero scenario is FIFA World Cup 2026 post-match egress at BMO Field.

Highlights:
- Built on the committed Toronto road graph (27,411 nodes / 73,036 directed edges), recolored by the assignment engine rather than canned data.
- cuGraph SSSP assignment backend and cuDF data pipeline tuned on the GB10 (aarch64), with an adaptive "blast-radius" recompute for local edits.
- A PyTorch/PyG graph neural network for traffic-demand prediction.
- A Nemotron copilot (via Ollama) that turns natural-language intent into validated, bylaw-checked tool calls using local RAG over Toronto bylaws.
- Two-mode web app: Simulate (3D camera + timeline to scrub the matchday) and Edit (top-down workspace).

Won 1st at the NVIDIA Spark Hack.
